source_refs.note: Book p. 277: 14.3.4 Properties of Cross Product (i)-(v); property (ii) printed without its minus sign; proofs left to students.

blocks.text: The cross product possesses the following properties:

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Property (ii) is printed as \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = \underline{v} \times \underline{u}\); the minus sign is missing. The correct property is \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -(\underline{v} \times \underline{u})\), as derived in 14.3.3 (c).
The proofs of these properties are left as an exercise for the students.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Short reasons for each property (our notes):
(i) If one vector is \(\underline{0}\), its length is 0, so \(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta = 0\).
(ii) Same length, but the right hand rule reverses the direction when the order is reversed (14.3.3 (c)).
(iii) The cross product distributes over addition, like ordinary multiplication; it can be checked with components (14.3.5). It is used in 14.3.5 to obtain the determinant formula.
(iv) Here \(k\) is a scalar. Multiplying a vector by \(k\) multiplies its length by \(|k|\) (and reverses it if \(k < 0\)), so the cross product is multiplied by \(k\).
(v) The angle between \(\underline{u}\) and itself is \(0\) and \(\sin 0 = 0\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
One property that does NOT hold: the cross product is not associative. For example
\[(\underline{i} \times \underline{i}) \times \underline{j} = \underline{0} \times \underline{j} = \underline{0}\]
\[\underline{i} \times (\underline{i} \times \underline{j}) = \underline{i} \times \underline{k} = -\underline{j}\]
So brackets in a repeated cross product must never be moved.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -(\underline{v} \times \underline{u})\): not commutative.
2. Distributive: \(\underline{u} \times (\underline{v} + \underline{w}) = \underline{u} \times \underline{v} + \underline{u} \times \underline{w}\).
3. Scalars come out: \(\underline{u} \times (k\underline{v}) = k(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\).
4. \(\underline{u} \times \underline{u} = \underline{0}\), and \(\underline{u} \times \underline{0} = \underline{0}\).

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Copying property (ii) as printed without the minus sign.
2. Moving brackets: \((\underline{u} \times \underline{v}) \times \underline{w}\) is generally not equal to \(\underline{u} \times (\underline{v} \times \underline{w})\).
3. Changing the order of the vectors while expanding with property (iii): keep each first vector first.
